title: Squadron 42 Delayed to 2027 as Star Citizen Dev Blames GTA 6
description: Cloud Imperium Games delays Squadron 42 to Q2 2027, with studio boss Chris Roberts citing concerns about being overshadowed by GTA 6.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Squadron 42 Pushed Back to 2027

The gravitational pull of Rockstar Games' upcoming blockbuster continues to bend the gaming industry's release calendar. According to a recent report by Eurogamer, Cloud Imperium Games has officially delayed the long-in-development Star Citizen spin-off, Squadron 42, to the second quarter of 2027.

The project, which has been in development for many years, is adjusting its timeline to ensure it gets adequate breathing room in a crowded market landscape.

## Chris Roberts Cites GTA 6 Concerns

When addressing the reasons behind the delay, studio boss Chris Roberts pointed directly to the looming presence of Grand Theft Auto 6. Roberts argued that launching the title too close to GTA 6 would risk the game being completely drowned out by the massive wave of attention surrounding Rockstar's upcoming masterpiece.

Given the unprecedented level of anticipation, media coverage, and consumer spending power commanded by the GTA franchise, developers across the industry are clearly recalibrating their launch strategies. Roberts' comments highlight the reality that even major, highly anticipated projects must carefully pick their battles to avoid competing directly with what is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of the decade.

## Looking Ahead to Q2 2027

While fans of the Star Citizen universe will need to exercise more patience as they await the single-player campaign's arrival in Q2 2027, the extra development time combined with a clearer release window away from the GTA shadow may ultimately benefit the game's launch.

## Editor's Take

Chris Roberts' candid admission underscores just how much influence GTA 6 holds over industry planning long before its release. Stepping out of the path of a juggernaut like GTA 6 is a pragmatic survival strategy for any studio, and we may see more developers adjusting their windows as the release approaches.
